idiom_name: protocol existentials + conditional casts (as?/is); protocol extension defaults
implementation_notes: The extension contract is a protocol and the query is a conditional cast: if let ta = component as? TextAccessor performs a runtime conformance check, protocol composition (Component & TextAccessor) expresses an extended view in a signature, and protocol extensions supply default implementations so a shipped protocol can gain members without breaking conformers. Nothing can retroactively conform a type you do not own, so an extension for a foreign type is an adapter value that conforms to the protocol and forwards to it, or the capability is handed back alongside the object; where the interface is name-driven rather than type-driven, @dynamicMemberLookup (SE-0195, Swift 4.2) turns component.word into subscript(dynamicMember:) - the lookup form of the same intent - with keypath-based lookup (SE-0252, Swift 5.1) adding static checking of member paths.
pitfalls: Protocol extension members are statically dispatched: an extension method is not overridden through the protocol, and a concrete-typed reference can silently call the protocol-extension implementation instead of the conformer's own method.
as? is a conformance test, not a contents test: a type can conform with an implementation that fails at run time, and the conformance must be visible in the module that performs the cast.
@dynamicMemberLookup must be declared on the type definition itself, not in an extension, so it cannot be retrofitted onto an existing type (SE-0195 explicitly rejected retroactive conformance).
An adapter holds the subject: caching it on the subject creates a retain cycle if the adapter captures it strongly.
